page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g-120s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The hardware configuration is completed by 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and 120 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU is included in this configuration.

Benchmark results show a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng CPU tests and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3. However, multi-core performance is weak, as evidenced by low scores in multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth for large blocks and static web serving throughput remain average, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and multi-threaded compiling tasks fall into the lower performance tier.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-threaded execution, this server offers a cost-effective profile for workloads that do not require massive parallelization. It is well-suited for lightweight static web serving, text processing, and basic single-threaded utility scripts. It is less optimal for highly concurrent database systems, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or complex LLM inference tasks.
